title: Best Badminton Shuttlecocks in India (2026)
summary: Three Decathlon India shuttlecock packs: one plastic, two feather. Based on product pages and maker advice, not hand-tested.
description: For badminton players in India choosing between plastic and feather shuttlecocks. Explains speed numbers and compares three Decathlon packs.
lead: Which shuttlecock should you buy for badminton in India? This guide looks at three Decathlon India packs: one plastic pack and two Kuikma feather packs. We have not hand-tested any of them. We read the Decathlon India product pages, Decathlon's advice page, the BWF Laws of Badminton and a Yonex page on cap colours. The product pages are short. They list the pack size, speed, rating, warranty and return terms, but not the feather or cork type. So we use Decathlon's advice page to explain the choice, and we say where a detail is missing. Stock changes often, so check the Decathlon India page before you buy.

picks.verdict: A plastic shuttle pack that fits casual games, going by Decathlon's own advice. The product page has very few details.
paragraphs: The PSC 100x6 is a plastic shuttle sold in a pack of 6, in yellow. The page title says Medium. Decathlon sells it under its own brand. The page shows a Made in India badge and says it is sold and fulfilled by Decathlon Sports India.

The page shows a 2 year warranty and a 30 days return option. The rating is 4.5 out of 5 from 225 reviews, but we could not see the review text. The page has no description, so we cannot tell you the head type, the weight or how long a shuttle lasts. Decathlon's advice page suggests a durable plastic shuttle for casual weekend play with family and friends. It also says plastic and feather shuttles fly differently.

choose.heading: Plastic or feather
choose.text: Decathlon's advice page says new and occasional players need a shuttle that can take repeated practice. For casual weekend play with family and friends, it suggests a durable plastic shuttle. For regular players, it suggests natural feather with mixed cork. For advanced players, it suggests goose feather with full cork. It also says plastic and feather shuttles have different flight paths.

choose.heading: Check your event rules
choose.text: The BWF Laws of Badminton say a shuttle may be made of natural or synthetic materials, or both. They say its flight should be similar to a natural feather shuttle. Which shuttle your own event uses is up to the organiser, so ask before you buy. This is general advice.

choose.heading: Understand the speed number
choose.text: Decathlon's advice page says labels such as 76 to 79, or 1 to 4, show the weight. A lower number means a lighter, slower shuttle. A higher number means a heavier, faster one. It says lighter shuttles suit hot, humid or high-altitude places. Heavier ones suit cold, dry or low-altitude places.

choose.heading: Colour caps on nylon shuttles
choose.text: Some nylon shuttles show speed by colour. For its Mavis 350, Yonex says the green cap is slow (about 22 to 33 degrees C), blue is medium (about 12 to 23 degrees C) and red is fast (about 0 to 13 degrees C). That is Yonex's own chart. The Decathlon plastic pick says Medium in its title, but its page gives no temperature range. So do not assume the Yonex chart applies to it.

choose.heading: Do a quick speed check
choose.text: The BWF Laws test shuttle speed with a full underhand stroke from over the back boundary line. The shuttle is hit upward and parallel to the side lines. A shuttle of correct speed lands 530 mm to 990 mm short of the other back boundary line. You can try the same stroke on your court. If the shuttle lands well short, a faster one may suit you. If it goes past the line, a slower one may suit you. That last part is our own suggestion, not a rule.

choose.heading: Check pack size, stock and approval
choose.text: The plastic pick has 6 shuttles and the two feather picks have 12 each. Stock changes often, so check the Decathlon India page before you plan a purchase. The product pages did not list any approval or feather and cork details. If these matter to you, check the pack itself or ask your event organiser.

faq.q: Should a beginner buy plastic or feather shuttlecocks?
faq.a: Decathlon's advice page says new players need a shuttle that can take repeated practice. For casual outdoor play, it suggests a durable plastic one. Feather shuttles fly differently, so some players move to them later.

faq.q: Can I use a plastic shuttlecock in a tournament?
faq.a: The BWF Laws allow a shuttle made of natural or synthetic materials if its flight is similar to a feather shuttle. Which type an event uses is the organiser's choice. Ask them before you buy. This is general advice.

faq.q: Which speed should I choose for India?
faq.a: Decathlon's advice page gives the direction but no fixed numbers. Use a lighter, lower-number shuttle in high heat, high humidity or at high altitude. Use a heavier, higher-number one in cold, dry places. Our two feather picks list only speed 76, so check that against your court. The BWF underhand check in this guide can help.

faq.q: What do green, blue and red caps mean?
faq.a: On Yonex nylon shuttles such as the Mavis 350, Yonex says green is slow, blue is medium and red is fast. Its page gives a temperature range for each. Other makers may use colours differently.

faq.q: How long does a feather shuttlecock last?
faq.a: We found no reliable figure on the pages we read, so we do not give one. How long a shuttle lasts depends on how you play and how you store it.
